turns.content: Order floor(n^(1/8)), floor(n^(1/7)), ..., floor(n^(1/2)). If all seven values are distinct, what minimum spacing between successive integer values follows?

Let b=floor(n^(1/8)). Translate that spacing into lower bounds b,b+1,...,b+6 for the eighth- through second-root floors, and convert them into power lower bounds for n. Also record the upper bound implied by floor(n^(1/8))=b.
Write the joint lower threshold as the maximum of b^8,(b+1)^7,(b+2)^6,(b+3)^5,(b+4)^4,(b+5)^3,(b+6)^2. Explain why satisfying only one of these bounds would be insufficient.
Using the current ladder, compare the eighth-root upper bound with the strongest required lower bound. Can this case occur?
Evaluate all seven power bounds for b and take their maximum. What is the least candidate n in this case, and does it respect the corresponding eighth-root upper bound?
Consider the remaining cases. Use the relevant power lower bounds and the candidate threshold from the b=2 analysis to decide whether any can produce a smaller valid n.
Directly compute the floors of the square through eighth roots of the candidate, and check that n itself is distinct from all of them.
State the smallest positive integer n and list the eight distinct quantities in the order requested.
